title: Post-hoc physical response and diffusion-horizon audit
status: Post-hoc diagnostic motivated by the original noisy study and known finite-memory cutoff theory. This is not an independent held-out discovery test.
fit_changes: none; evaluate already accepted regularized matrices
units: beta=mass=1; dimensionless time, frequency and diffusivity
response_definition: stationary mean velocity amplitude per additive force for F(t)=Re(F0 exp(i omega t))
error_measure: maximum complex relative mobility error per logarithmically sampled band; summaries conditional on prior acceptance
interpretation: Numerical horizons are first grid-point exceedances, not uniform confidence bounds.
Normal-diffusion asymptotics require finite real stable full and auxiliary matrices; singular auxiliary blocks are explicit exceptions.
The fractional target has no physical low-frequency cutoff by construction; a real material may have one.
Equilibrium linear response is fixed by the exact all-time VACF. These are predicted response diagnostics, not measured forces or evidence for new physics.
